For categories where no evidence of constraint exists, explicitly note 'no evidence of constraint at current scale' rather than leaving it unchecked. Any genuine finding deserves a concrete, specific fix, directly extending this curriculum's repeated insistence that the most reliable data architecture decisions are always direct, systematic, and evidence-grounded.

checkpoints.question: A review finds an ETL pipeline uses idempotent UPSERT loading but persists its cursor only at the end of each complete run, not per-batch. Is this a genuine finding, and what is the specific risk?
options: This is not a genuine finding; end-of-run cursor persistence is always equivalent to per-batch persistence

Yes, this is a genuine finding - a mid-run failure forces the next restart to reprocess from the beginning rather than from the last completed batch, which is unnecessarily expensive and potentially slow for large datasets, even though idempotent loading makes it safe
End-of-run cursor persistence is always preferable to per-batch persistence
Cursor persistence has no relationship to pipeline restart behavior

codingChallenge.title: Conduct A Complete, Five-Category Data Architecture Review With Evidence-Based Conclusions
codingChallenge.description: Given evidence about a growing application's data characteristics, conduct this module's complete five-category review, identifying genuine findings and correctly concluding 'not yet needed' where evidence doesn't support a layer.
codingChallenge.solutionExample:
## DATA ARCHITECTURE REVIEW: SaaS Analytics Tool

### 1. Write Throughput Audit:
MEASURED: 200 writes/second at peak.
PostgreSQL capacity: ~15,000 writes/second.
CONCLUSION: No evidence of write constraint (200/15,000 = 1.3%
capacity). Sharding NOT warranted at current scale.

### 2. Read Throughput Audit:
MEASURED: 5,000 reads/second; primary at 25% CPU from reads.
CONCLUSION: Primary showing measurable read load impact. At least
1 read replica recommended to offload transactional reads. Monitor
for growth - as read load increases, additional replicas may follow.

### 3. Pipeline Reliability Audit:
GENUINE FINDING: full-table extraction on 80M-row source table.
Pipeline now takes 45 minutes for each hourly run - nearly the
entire scheduling window, and will exceed it as the table grows.
FIX: migrate to cursor-based incremental extraction (lesson 3).
Also check: is the LOAD step using idempotent UPSERT? (not specified)

### 4. Analytical Performance Audit:
GENUINE FINDING: analytical queries taking 30-90 seconds on a
row-oriented PostgreSQL replica. Full sequential scans confirmed
(EXPLAIN analysis needed to verify).
FIX: migrate analytical queries to a column-oriented OLAP system.
This is also the correct fix to relieve the read replica of
heavy analytical scan load.

### 5. Schema Organization Audit:
NOT YET APPLICABLE: no OLAP system exists. Once OLAP is in
place (finding 4's fix), design star schema around the specific
analytical questions users actually need to answer.

## SUMMARY: 2 genuine findings (pipeline extraction, OLAP migration).
## 1 recommendation (read replica). Write throughput: correctly
## 'not needed'. Star schema: deferred until OLAP is established.
validationRules: Write throughput must be concluded as 'not warranted at current scale' with specific evidence (200 vs 15,000 writes/second)
Read throughput must identify a genuine finding with specific evidence (25% CPU from reads) and recommend read replicas
Pipeline must identify full-table extraction as a genuine finding with cursor-based extraction as the specific fix
Analytical performance must identify a genuine finding and recommend OLAP migration
Star schema must be correctly deferred until the OLAP system exists, not recommended as an immediate action
hints: Write throughput at 1.3% of capacity is definitively 'no evidence of constraint' - this is exactly the kind of conclusion this module's evidence-first discipline should produce
The star schema recommendation must be sequenced AFTER the OLAP migration - you can't properly design a star schema without first having a column-oriented system to put it in
The pipeline finding is the most operationally urgent - a 45-minute extraction for an hourly run is already nearly unsustainable and will break completely as the table grows

finalModuleProject.title: Design And Justify A Complete Data Architecture For A Growing Application
finalModuleProject.goal: Synthesize all six lessons into one complete, evidence-justified data architecture: apply the bottleneck discipline, design a replication/sharding strategy, build a reliable ETL pipeline, select and justify an OLAP system, design a star schema, and conduct a five-category production review of your own design.
finalModuleProject.description: Choose an application context (your own Module 26 capstone, a hypothetical e-commerce platform, or a SaaS tool) and build its complete data architecture: identify which of the four data bottleneck types (read throughput, write throughput, analytical performance, analytical organization) your application genuinely faces with specific evidence; design a replication strategy (how many read replicas, justified by measured read load) and explicitly evaluate whether write sharding is warranted; build a complete incremental ETL pipeline with cursor-based extraction and idempotent loading, verified by tracing its restart behavior explicitly; select an OLAP system for analytical queries and demonstrate the query performance difference with a specific worked example; design a star schema with at least one fact table and two dimension tables specifically chosen to support three named analytical questions; and conduct the five-category production review of your own design, correctly concluding 'not yet needed' for any layer not supported by evidence.

requirements.requirement: A bottleneck analysis identifying which of the four data constraint types your application genuinely faces, with specific measured or estimated evidence for each conclusion
A replication strategy with the number of read replicas justified by evidence, and an explicit, evidence-based conclusion about whether write sharding is warranted
A complete ETL pipeline with cursor-based extraction, idempotent UPSERT loading, and per-batch cursor persistence, with an explicit restart-behavior trace
An OLAP system selection with a specific worked query demonstrating the performance difference versus a row-oriented replica
A star schema with at least one fact table and two dimension tables, with columns chosen specifically to support three named analytical questions
A complete five-category production review of your own design, with evidence-based conclusions for each category including 'not yet needed' where appropriate

rubric.criterion: Bottleneck analysis correctly identifies genuine constraints with specific evidence, and correctly concludes 'not yet needed' for layers without evidence
Replication strategy is evidence-justified, and sharding conclusion (yes or no) is supported by specific write load evidence
ETL pipeline correctly implements cursor-based extraction, idempotent loading, and per-batch checkpointing, verified by explicit restart trace
OLAP system selection includes a specific, worked query comparison demonstrating the structural performance difference
Star schema columns are specifically chosen to support the three named analytical questions, with fact/dimension distinction correctly applied
Five-category review is systematic, evidence-based, and correctly sequences deferred recommendations
